compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Taskmaster utilizes logical data segregation to isolate customer data from other customers.   Customer data is not stored at rest other than account holders name, email, account number - references to scheduled items (itemId) are stored in memory during the process of scheduling but not persisted.    Tokens are encrypted in transit and at rest (AES256) - these are accessed logically by decoding the users JWT sessionToken.

Infrastructure is provided by Vercel who have a robust method of patching and updating.   Database is provided by Mongo Atlas, serverless (also managed)

Code analysis and security is provided by Dependabot, code is not able to be commited into production without passing its scanning tools.  Additional alerting is setup for vulnerabilities.  
Dependabot alerts—inform you about vulnerabilities in the dependencies that you use in your repository.
Dependabot security updates—automatically raise pull requests to update the dependencies you use that have known security vulnerabilities.
Dependabot version updates—automatically raise pull requests to keep your dependencies up-to-date.

Critical: We strive to patch critical vulnerabilities within 24 hours of their disclosure or discovery. This includes deploying a fix or mitigating the vulnerability to minimize potential impact.
High: High-severity vulnerabilities are addressed with high urgency. We aim to patch them within 48 hours of disclosure or discovery.
Medium: We address medium-severity vulnerabilities within a timeframe of 7 business days. This timeframe allows for thorough testing and evaluation of the patch before deployment.
Low: Low-severity vulnerabilities are patched within a reasonable timeframe, typically within 30 business days. The exact timeframe may depend on the availability of a patch and the potential impact of the vulnerability.

Taskmaster takes data security very seriously. In the unfortunate event of a security breach that may impact monday.com or its users, we have a clear communication protocol in place to notify them promptly.

Notification Timeline:

Immediate action: Upon detection or suspicion of a security breach, Taskmaster will initiate an internal investigation to determine the scope and nature of the incident. This includes containing the breach, mitigating potential damage, and preserving evidence.
Within 24 hours: Once the initial assessment is complete, Taskmaster will notify monday.com security team directly through their designated point of contact. This notification will include the following information:
Nature and scope of the breach (if known)
Affected systems or data
Potential impact on monday.com users
Mitigation steps already taken
Next steps and timeline for further investigation and remediation
We utilise the accessToken/sessionToken of the user to authenticate state changing actions.
We typically do not utilise untrusted data sources, where we do we utilise reactjs components that carry this sanitisation process out.
As stated before, customer data is extremely limited.  However DB access (prod) is tightly controlled with access only provided to the production app, and myself (Owner)
2FA Auth is required into the Database system control pane, with certificates required to API access.
New Relic is used with obfuscation and drop rules set to drop the sessionTokens from logs.
Input validation via the ReactJS Components is provided (as previously stated) - server side endpoints however as also validated prior to processing.
The only redirect present is via the oAuth flow which is controlled.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer:
We apply logical separation in our databases and file-storage. Each customer has a unique "customerID" which is passed to all database-queries. MongoDB-collections are indexed by this customerID. For file-storage, we store customer-related files in their own directory (using that customerID).
API-calls usually require the CustomerID to retrieve/post data. The API-key needed to make API-calls is also registered with a specific CustomerID.

Most critical systems apply auto-upgrading, like our managed GKE cluster (GCP's Kubernetes Engine) and our MongoDB Atlas clusters.
We use container-optimized OS-es in our GKE cluster, which are auto-patched on the OS-level.
PRs for dependency-patches are done automatically via Renovate (similar to Github's Dependabot).

If we notice a customer is affected by a security breach, we notify the customer. If needed, we also notify the AP (Dutch Data Protection Authority) as required by GDPR.
If a security specifically hits customers that use our monday-integration, we will notify monday.com as well.

We use your official monday-sdk to grab a sessionToken provided when navigating from your settings page.
This sessionToken is passed along to our server on each request, for server-side validation.
We sanitize all user inputs before performing MongoDB queries. We also apply schema-validation on all requests to our server.

By default, only our operational Dev-team has access to the database(s) with customer data.
Administrative / superuser access is only applied to individuals, not using shared accounts.
Access to our systems processing customer data is only available to the operational Dev-team, using a user-specific login requiring 2FA and a VPN-connection.

We have strict guidelines on what to log, and it's part of our PR review process to be very strict in that: only log what needs to be logged.
We make sure we keep user-data out of URLs that are posted to the server, as this would end up in access-logs.
Our monday-app does not rely on such auto-binding / ORM-layers. We sanitize requests using schema-validation, and make case-specific MongoDB-queries.

We ensure no "user input" is used to make redirects.
We also setup a very strict CSP to only allow loading scripts, images, and styles from our own server.
We're a Dutch (EU) company, so we have to comply with GDPR by law. Next to that, we are ISO27001 and ISO27701 (Privacy module) certified.
We are ISO27001 + ISO27701 certified though. We're thinking of adding SOC2 next year though as this helps to expand in the US where SOC2 is more common than ISO27001.
HIPAA is very much US-centered. This is not (yet) relevant for us.
djhoek@moreapp.com
Periodic pen-test is required by the ISO27001 norm. We've set our interval to "at least once a year".

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer:
We use Logical Segregation:

Tenant IDs: Each customer's data is tagged with a unique tenant ID, ensuring that our access controls strictly enforce that users can only access data belonging to their tenant.

Our patching time frames are designed to address vulnerabilities based on their severity and potential impact on our service and customers. The time frames are as follows:

Critical Vulnerabilities: Within 24 hours of identification.
These vulnerabilities pose an immediate threat to the security and stability of our systems and could lead to significant data breaches or service disruptions. They are addressed with the highest priority and expedited through our patching process.

High Vulnerabilities: Within 1 week of identification.
Serious vulnerabilities, that could potentially be exploited to cause significant harm, are prioritized and patched as quickly as possible after thorough testing.

Medium Vulnerabilities: Within 1 month of identification.
Those of lower risk of exploitation are scheduled for regular patching cycles and addressed in a timely manner.

Low Vulnerabilities: Within 3 months of identification.
These vulnerabilities pose minimal risk and are addressed during routine maintenance and update cycles. They are patched to ensure ongoing security hygiene and compliance.

In the event of a security breach, we will immediately contain the breach and prevent further unauthorized access. monday.com will be notified within 24 hours of detecting the breach, providing a brief overview of the incident via email or phone. Within 48 hours, a detailed report will be submitted, including a description of the breach, its impact, containment measures, and mitigation steps. We will keep monday.com regularly updated on the progress of the investigation and provide a final report upon resolution.
We implement a strict Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy to ensure that only trusted origins (monday.com) can interact with our API, further reducing the risk of CSRF attacks.

Input Validation and Sanitization:

Server-Side Validation: All user inputs are validated on the server side to ensure they meet the expected format and constraints. We use libraries and frameworks that provide built-in sanitization functions to remove or neutralize potentially harmful code.
Client-Side Validation: While server-side validation is the primary defense, we also implement client-side validation to provide immediate feedback to users and reduce the load on the server.

Escaping and Encoding:

Input Encoding: Before using user-supplied data, we encode the input to ensure that any HTML special characters are properly escaped. 

Using Trusted Libraries:

DOMPurify: For HTML sanitization, we use DOMPurify, a library that cleans HTML by removing malicious code while preserving valid content. It is used to sanitize any HTML input before rendering it in the browser.
Other Libraries: We leverage other trusted libraries and frameworks that provide built-in XSS protection features, such as React's automatic escaping of strings in JSX and Angular's built-in XSS protection.

We use Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) like:

Access Levels: We implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to ensure that employees only have access to the data necessary for their job functions. Access levels are determined based on roles such as administrator, developer, support staff, and other relevant positions.
Principle of Least Privilege: Employees are granted the minimum level of access required to perform their duties. This minimizes the risk of unauthorized access to customer data.

We use the following:

Selective Logging:

Logging Policies: We have strict logging policies that dictate what types of information can and cannot be logged. These policies ensure that only non-sensitive, operational data is recorded in logs.
Minimal Logging: We adhere to the principle of minimal logging, capturing only the essential information required for troubleshooting and performance monitoring, thereby reducing the risk of logging sensitive data.

Environment-Specific Logging:

Development and Production: We differentiate between logging in development and production environments. In development, more detailed logs might be necessary, but we ensure they do not contain any real user data. In production, logs are carefully monitored and controlled to exclude any secrets or PII.
Where possible, we disable or limit mass assignment features within our ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) libraries.
We avoid using direct user input for redirect destinations. Instead, we map user actions to predefined, trusted URLs.
marc@doc2board.com

Yes, our logging practices are designed to exclude secrets and personally identifiable information (PII). We adhere to best practices for log management, limiting log entries to essential parameters.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: In our system, customer data is segregated using logical separation techniques to ensure privacy and security. Each piece of data is associated explicitly with a user through their unique user_id and account_id. This is evident in our database schema for the oauth_tokens table, where both user_id and account_id serve as a composite primary key. This design ensures that access tokens and related information are uniquely tied to individual user accounts, preventing data from being accessible across different users.

We continuously monitor for any new security patches or updates available for Python, React, and any other dependent libraries or frameworks used in our application. This includes subscribing to security bulletins and updates from trusted sources related to our technology stack.

For frontend we use npm audit for new patches every major iteration i.e each month.

Yes, our application rigorously enforces XSS encoding and sanitization on all user-supplied parameters to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. Here are the specific measures we've implemented:

Input Sanitization: We sanitize all inputs received from the users at the point of entry. This involves stripping out or encoding potentially dangerous characters and patterns that could be used in XSS attacks. Our backend, built with Python, uses libraries such as bleach to sanitize inputs before they are processed or stored.

Output Encoding: When displaying user input or data that could potentially include user input, we encode the output to prevent execution of unwanted scripts. For our frontend in React, we ensure that all dynamic content is rendered using safe functions that automatically escape HTML. React inherently escapes all strings inserted into the HTML by default, which provides a strong defense against XSS.

Content Security Policy (CSP): We implement a robust Content Security Policy that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including XSS and data injection attacks. By specifying valid sources of executable scripts and the types of scripts that can run or be loaded on our website, CSP serves as a secondary line of defense against XSS.

Use of Safe Libraries: We utilize frameworks and libraries that are known for their strong security practices. React, for example, provides XSS protection by escaping strings that are embedded in JSX before rendering them. This prevents malicious scripts from being inadvertently executed.
The customer secret is only accessible to the lead developer in this case company owner.
We don't store logs in our server , all customer logs are maintained in monday activity log itself.

Yes, we use AWS ECR for our API to containerize the images, which automatically gives us a security scan of the Docker Image and all packages within that image. We ensure to patch Critical, High, and Medium bugs as soon as they are discovered, and we address Low vulnerabilities within the next API update that we do, which is usually within a day or two.

I have a Security Runbook with step by step instructions in case of a security breach to reach out to monday.com

Security Breach Protocol

Background Information

Monitor AWS CloudTrail, Cloudwatch, and other reporting mechanisms to observe network traffic and AWS resource management for anything out of the ordinary. In the event there is a possible security breach, even a "feeling", we will make sure to rotate all keys and secrets for everyone in the account.

Steps in case of a Breach

Immediately rotate all AWS Keys in SecretsManager, IAM, and Github

Immediately rotate passwords for each AWS Account access

Immediately fill out a Support Ticket with monday.com and email them

https://support.monday.com/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=13855862562962

https://monday.com/helpcenter/contact-support?_ga=2.171170848.1277700123.1716697138-27270506.1680022566&_gac=1.156828361.1714329733.CjwKCAjw57exBhAsEiwAaIxaZoA0FAf_wmIK-0X4xngX0b8mxpUOWOXyjWJ1wwv1hbCxwrOJg5WY5RoChecQAvD_BwE



Email Template:


Dear monday.com,

We are contacting you on behalf of SecureChat, an application listed on the monday.com app store. We have realized there was a security breach within our internal systems and we have taken the following actions:


Rotated all keys and passwords

Identified the threat and the resources they have accessed

Removed the bad actor/ vendor and terminated services

Please reach out to alexander@revapps.io for additional information so we can further discuss.

All the best,

We have an internal token that we verify upon every single state changing API request that is explicitly set into client side state and nowhere else. Our API sets this CSRF protection token in the headers upon user authentication, then validates it for any HTTPS POST, PATCH, and DELETE request.

On the client side we use DOMpurify with React to sanitize the inputs, and on the API side we use AWS WAF (Web Access Firewall) with several rules to validate requests, including a subscription for XSS protection for the WAF.

The two founders of the company and our software engineer, who has a valid employment contract with RevApps Incorporated, are the only people who have access to our AWS Account, which contains customer data.
We use AWS SSO with enforced MFA (and other password strength requirements) for our AWS Accounts, which contain customer data. MFA is enforced at the login level and is required every 8 hours.

Yes, we implemented Winston (a popular Node.js npm package) configured to ensure no secrets or PII are ever logged into AWS Cloudwatch. This logger configuration is set up for our ECS Service and Lambda functions.

All user supplied parameters (accountId, userId, etc) are validated with the JWT after it has been verified. If there is any discrepancy, we simply return a 401 response code. There are no "default trusted parameters", we always verify each API call with the JWT.
On our client side, any redirect will create a standard Alert in the browser warning them of leaving the site. The only domains that are listed as trusted are "monday.com" and "revapps.io"
We have all terms listed in our Privacy Policy and Terms of Service, ensure that only data collected is for the business needs of the app.
Not yet- we can provide a letter of attestation from our security vendor, Drata, that we are actively working towards SOC 2 compliance.
Not yet- we also plan on working with Drata to achieve this.

Follow the principle of least privilege, granting employees only the permissions necessary to perform their job duties. Ensure that access controls are implemented at both the operating system and database levels to restrict access to sensitive data.

Implement user activity monitoring to track and log employee actions within systems processing customer data. Monitor for any suspicious or unauthorized activity that may indicate a security breach or insider threat.

5. Security Awareness Training:
Provide comprehensive security awareness training for employees to educate them about the importance of protecting customer data and the risks associated with unauthorized access. Include training on identifying phishing attempts, social engineering tactics, and other common security threats.

6. Encryption:
Implement encryption for data at rest and in transit to protect customer data from unauthorized access in the event of a security breach or unauthorized access.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer:
Customer data is segregated using a PostgreSQL database (through Supabase) and tables within that database. Requests to access this data are validated using the authenticated monday.com user's session token then routed to the appropriate table and row in the table. 

Here's more on how Supabase handles customer data: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/secure-data

Application-level updates and patches are handled via a continuous integration pipeline. When an update is needed, the code change is applied and pushed to a repository on Github. For the server, the push results in an new deployment of the backend server. For the iframe app, a zip file is created and uploaded.
In the event of a security breach, monday will be notified via email immediately.

The monday app is an iframed sandbox app with no direct access to the parent window. This helps prevent any state-changing actions via CSRF. The iframe communicates directly with a backend server and that is it.
There are no user freeform inputs to sanitize.
This is a solo business, and I am the only employee.
This is a solo business, and I have MFA enabled for all resources.

The backend logging is done through Cloudflare Logpush which allows fine-grained control of the logs sent. The app removes any PII as part of the logging. 

https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/logging/logpush/
The app does not have any freeform user inputs to enable this.
The only redirect allowed by the app is during the OAuth flow and that is scoped to the defined Redirect URI in the monday developer portal.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Yes we are segregating customer data on basis of different monday accounts. Each monday org's data is stored segregated to others.

We are using JWT Token for CSRF protection
1. Generate JWT Token:
Upon successful authentication (e.g., user login), a JSON Web Token (JWT) is generated.
The token is created using a secret key and includes a payload with user-specific information and claims.
2. Send JWT Token in API Calls:
For each subsequent API request, the generated JWT token is included in the HTTP header.
Typically, the token is placed in the Authorization header using the Bearer schema.

We are using Helmet and sanitize package on the backend to perform XSS encoding and protect our app against malicious attacks.

Sanitizing Input Data in API Requests
1. Extracting Data from req.body or req.params:
When handling incoming API requests, data can be extracted from req.body (for POST requests) or req.params (for GET requests).
2. Sanitizing Extracted Data:
To prevent security vulnerabilities such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), or other malicious attacks, it is crucial to sanitize all user inputs.
Sanitization involves cleaning the data to remove or neutralize any potentially harmful content.
3. Sanitization Before Database Interaction:
Before using the sanitized data to interact with the database, ensure that it is safe and free from any harmful code or injections.
Libraries and frameworks offer built-in methods or third-party packages to assist in sanitizing input data.

Only the company classified team have the access to the customer data. These classified members are from product development and management team. Cloud Analogy takes whole responsibility for the same.
We are using MongoDB database for storing the customer data and we have enabled their standard two factor authentication feature.

In our solution, we ensure that logs do not contain secrets and personally identifiable information (PII) by not actively managing or storing any logs. By abstaining from logging altogether, we eliminate the risk of inadvertently capturing or exposing sensitive data in log files. This approach simplifies our data management practices and mitigates the need for implementing additional measures such as redaction, access controls, or encryption of log data. Furthermore, by not logging any information, we adhere to strict data protection principles and maintain a streamlined approach to our operational security practices.

1. Explicitly Specify Allowed Parameters
When destructuring objects in JavaScript, ensure that you explicitly specify only the parameters that are safe and necessary for your operation.

2. Validation and Sanitization
Validate and sanitize all incoming data before using it. Libraries like Joi or express-validator can help with this.

3. Use Middleware for Input Filtering
Implement middleware to filter incoming requests and allow only specific fields to pass through.
Not applicable as we are not redirecting the user to any untrusted content.

Security Incidents are identified by logger and in the event of a security breach, we would notify monday.com promptly following these steps:

Immediate Detection and Assessment: As soon as a security breach is detected, we assesses the scope and impact of the breach.

Initial Notification: Within 48 hours of confirming a security breach, we will notify monday.com through the designated communication channel, providing preliminary details about the incident.

Detailed Report: A comprehensive report detailing the nature of the breach, affected data, and initial mitigation steps will be sent to monday.com.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: User data is logically separated in the database within a multi-tenant architecture. We use access control mechanisms to ensure that each user can only access their own data.

We use AWS to automatically patch and update our databases and services. Application level updates and backend patches are managed through Snyk: critical vulnerabilities are addressed immediately, high within a week, and medium and low within a month.
As soon as we become aware of a security breach, we will contact the monday.com team and notify them by email.
We use the JWT token provided by monday.com to authorise each client in our application. The token is added as an authorisation header. This protects our users from CSRF attacks.

We use React for our frontend, which inherently protects against XSS attacks by escaping all user-supplied input before rendering it in the DOM. This built-in protection ensures that user input is sanitised and properly encoded.
Only the CEO has access to customer data, and this access is protected by an encrypted connection and enforced security policies within a private network.
All employees are required to use multi-factor authentication (MFA) in addition to password login. All corporate applications are configured with single sign-on (SSO).

We do not store PII information in logs and use a single logger across the system, following best practices to limit parameters. In addition, we perform code reviews on all code that goes into production to ensure compliance.

The application protects against mass parameterisation attacks by rigorously validating input data to ensure that only permitted fields are processed, and by explicitly specifying which fields can be updated to prevent unauthorised changes.
We only use redirects to our own servers.
artem@setupsolution.io

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer:
We store three types of data:
Data required for proper synchronization: This includes only IDs and timestamps.
Account details (account slug and user’s email): We obtain these from app events to resolve payment issues. These details are deleted if users uninstall the integration.
Access tokens: These are used to perform the actual synchronization. Access tokens are encoded before being saved in the database and removed when users uninstall the integration.
The DB is encrypted by default using the built-in AWS tools. The encryption token is saved separately from DB.

We are using AWS as infrastructure: it takes care for DB updates. There are enabled, and any security patch will be applied by the AWS itself.
For the app itself, we are using Dependabot tool in Github, to notify us about any security updates in dependent packages. So the security patches will be applies as soon as we get a notification.

We will restrict access to AWS systems and any unusual activity will be reported to Naveed Choudhury. These will then be forward to monday.com.

 1. Initial Notification. We will notify monday.com within 24 hours of detecting a security breach. The initial notification will be sent via email. Alongside this email, this will also be escalated with the Partner Manager. The initial notification will include: (1) A brief description of the breach; (2) The potential impact on monday.com; (3) Immediate actions taken to mitigate the breach

2. Ongoing Updates. We will provide ongoing updates as we gather more information and as the situation evolves. Each update will include: (1) Latest findings and status of the breach; (2) Actions taken since the last update; (3) Next steps in our response plan

3. Post-Incident Report. Once the breach is contained and resolved, we will provide a detailed post-incident report. The report will include: (1) A detailed account of the breach: (2) Root cause analysis; (3) Steps taken to resolve the breach; and (4) Measures implemented to prevent future breaches
In all cases, whenever the app state is changed by a user, the app authorizes all requests with a monday.com session token. Changes can only be made through integration and cannot be forged.

React has a built-in mechanism to prevent this on the frontend. The app has no place to input any malicious scripts in the UI. To ensure security, the backend uses parameter filtering, sanitization, and session tokens.
Apps data is stored inside AWS. We use MFA to provide access to this data.
AWS MFA
The app logs errors, synchronization results, and monday.com app events. The only user information logged is accountId and userId.

All requests are verified using a session token. The app retrieves only the necessary parameters from the request before performing an action. The app sanitizes these parameters before putting their values into the database.
The app only redirects monday.com OAuth flow when getting a user's access token.

We are compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). By using our app, users acknowledge and agree to our collection, use, and sharing of their information as described in the Data Privacy Clause of our T&C, ensuring full compliance with GDPR. Our Terms and Conditions for app usage outline the data privacy policies of Mint, which align with the seven protection and accountability principles outlined in Article 5.1-2 of the GDPR.
N/A
We are not collecting any HIPAA-sensitive data.

marketplace_apps.description:
Manage TestRail test cases for your monday items right from the item UI. 


Forget about switching between monday and TestRail trying to remember which test case corresponds to which item and vice versa. After a test case is created, it will be shown as a link in the list of test cases right in your monday item. In TestRail, the test case will have a link pointing to the monday item, for which it has been created. So, you can easily track the connection between item and test case from both the systems.


The following features are supported:


ADDING TEST CASES TO TESTRAIL PROJECTS OF DIFFERENT STRUCTURE

You can add test cases to projects with multiple suites as well as to the projects without any suites.


ADDING TEST CASES FOR ANY HIERARCHY OF SECTIONS

Have your test cases organized across many sections (folders) in TestRail? All of them will be available to you, when creating a test case from monday


LINKING EXISTING TEST CASES FROM TESTRAIL

Test cases, initially created in TestRail, can be linked to monday items with just a couple of clicks


ANALYTICS FROM TESTRAIL

View testing status across projects, test plans and test runs. The app also allows to analyse test case results across multiple test runs.


TEST CASE TEMPLATES

Select any of your TestRail templates (BDD, steps, etc.) when creating a test case for your monday item


TYPES & PRIORITIES

Feature in your monday item should be tested from different angles? The app allows you to create the proper test cases for each of them. Of course, some of the tests will be more important than others. You can specify it by selecting priority when creating a test case.


REMOVAL OF TEST CASES

Something changed and a test case is not relevant anymore for your monday item? You can safely remove it from the item still keeping it in TestRail, just in case test results will be needed in future.


Prerequisite:

Before using the app, parameters for how to connect to TestRail should be specified in the app settings. Please refer to the How-To for more details


In case of any questions or to book a demo, please contact us at support@kilomray.com

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Software has a multi-tenant architecture. All customer data is segregated logically on the basis of the Account ID. Account ID is retrieved from application session.

Application leverages serverless NoSQL DB (AWS DynamoDB) which does not require updates from client.

Application code is built and deployed by a CICD pipeline.
GitHub Dependabot is used to keep package dependencies up to date.
ops42 has an incident management procedure in place to notify monday.com in case of a breach

All requests to backend are authenticated with monday.com token.
1. Backend application is verifying request token from monday.com using monday.com signing secret.

All user-supplied inputs are sanitized for XSS and validated.

Application has 2 sources of user-provided data:
1. Recipe input fields
2. File and folder names 

The application has the following measures built-in:
1. All data from recipe input fields is sanitized with DOMPurify
2. All user-managed data from Google Drive, like file and folder names is sanitized with DOMPurify
3. Freetext data for folder URL is validated to be a real URL with whitelisted domains

The company has only one employee.
User secrets like OAuth authentication tokens are encrypted with KMS key using client-side encryption.

Customer data is processed on AWS cloud. AWS Access is managed with SSO (AWS Identity Center) from Google Workspace.
Google workspace has 2-Factor authentication enforced.

AWS Root account has MFA set up.

Application logs are delivered to AWS Cloudwatch Logs log group. The log group has data protection policies enabled for automatic masking and reporting for all sensitive information findings.
Enabled policies: Credentials, PII, PHI, Financial information
The application does not have a user-facing interface (integration-only)
The application does not have a user-facing interface which makes redirects (integration-only)
The application is not storing PII or user data apart from usage information. Third-party processors are compliant with GDPR.
gennady.potapov@ops42.org

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: We store user accessTokens in the encrypted SecureStorage provided by and hosted on monday code. We store snoozed item information (boardId, itemId, etc) in an SQL database on supabase.
aidan@atomicapps.io

We store limited personal information, including user names and email addresses, in our Supabase database, which is GDPR-compliant. All data transfers outside of the European Economic Area (EEA) are protected by Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), and we have signed a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with Supabase to ensure the security and compliance of stored data. Users have rights under GDPR, including the right to access, correct, or request deletion of their data, which we honor in accordance with applicable regulations.
We do not log any secrets or PII. Our code and logs are both rigorously reviewed to ensure no secrets are logged and we do not currently store any personally identifiable information.

Atomic Apps applies the principle of least privilege to protect access to customer data. Access to personal information, such as user names and email addresses stored in our Supabase database, is strictly limited to only what is necessary for the operation and support of the Snooze App. Only authorized personnel have access to this data, and all access is controlled and monitored. Customer data is stored securely in compliance with GDPR.

We employ rigorous sanitization on all user inputs across our application to safeguard against XSS vulnerabilities. We use the 'sanitize-html' library to strip out all HTML tags and attributes from inputs, ensuring only clean, safe text is porcessed. This sanitization is applied to all POST requests before any processing occurs, directly in our Express middleware.

Our middleware intercepts every request and recursively sanitizes all strings in the query, body, and URL parameters. This ensures that no malicious script can execute if inserted into any input field. By strictly allowing no HTML content, we effectively neutralize potential XSS attacks, maintaining the integrity and security of user data and interactions.

In the event of a security breach, we will notify monday.com immediately upon discovery and confirmation of the incident. Communication will be made through the developer support channels. We commit to providing a preliminary report including the nature of the breach, the data affected, and the potential impact within 24 hours of the breach discovery.

Our app uses npm for dependency management & updates. All updates are rigorously tested on our staging environment before deployment to production and we adhere to semantic versioning.

Our time frames for applying patches to vulnerabilities are as follows:
- Critical Vulnerabilities: Patches applied within 48 hours
- High Vulnerabilities: Patches applied within one week
- Medium Vulnerabilities: Patches applied within two weeks
- Low Vulnerabilities: Patches applied within one month

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: OptiRoute utilizes logical data segregation to isolate customer data from other customers. Customer data is not stored at rest other than account holders name, email, account number - references to scheduled items (itemId, item name and location) are stored purely to display results back to the user.  Tokens are encrypted in transit and at rest (AES256) - these are accessed logically by decoding the users

Infrastructure is provided by Vercel who have a robust method of patching and updating. Database is provided by Mongo Atlas, serverless (also managed) Code analysis and security is provided by Dependabot, code is not able to be commited into production without passing its scanning tools. Additional alerting is setup for vulnerabilities. Dependabot alerts—inform you about vulnerabilities in the dependencies that you use in your repository. Dependabot security updates—automatically raise pull requests to update the dependencies you use that have known security vulnerabilities. Dependabot version updates—automatically raise pull requests to keep your dependencies up-to-date. Critical: We strive to patch critical vulnerabilities within 24 hours of their disclosure or discovery. This includes deploying a fix or mitigating the vulnerability to minimize potential impact. High: High-severity vulnerabilities are addressed with high urgency. We aim to patch them within 48 hours of disclosure or discovery. Medium: We address medium-severity vulnerabilities within a timeframe of 7 business days. This timeframe allows for thorough testing and evaluation of the patch before deployment. Low: Low-severity vulnerabilities are patched within a reasonable timeframe, typically within 30 business days. The exact timeframe may depend on the availability of a patch and the potential impact of the vulnerability.

Appd takes data security very seriously. In the unfortunate event of a security breach that may impact monday.com or its users, we have a clear communication protocol in place to notify them promptly. Notification Timeline: Immediate action: Upon detection or suspicion of a security breach, Appd will initiate an internal investigation to determine the scope and nature of the incident. This includes containing the breach, mitigating potential damage, and preserving evidence. Within 24 hours: Once the initial assessment is complete, Appd will notify monday.com security team directly through their designated point of contact. This notification will include the following information: Nature and scope of the breach (if known) Affected systems or data Potential impact on monday.com users Mitigation steps already taken Next steps and timeline for further investigation and remediation
We utilise the accessToken/sessionToken of the user to authenticate state changing actions.
We typically do not utilise untrusted data sources, where we do we utilise reactjs components that carry this sanitisation process out.
New Relic is used with obfuscation and drop rules set to drop the sessionTokens from logs.
Input validation via the ReactJS Components is provided (as previously stated) - server side endpoints however as also validated prior to processing.
The only redirect present is via the oAuth flow which is controlled.

The app ensures safe redirects and forwards by implementing an allow list of trusted destinations. Before performing a redirect, the app checks the target URL against this allow list to verify it is an approved location.

Yes, the app protects against mass parameter assignment attacks by implementing strong parameter filtering and whitelisting. Only explicitly permitted fields are allowed to be updated when handling user input, preventing unauthorized or unintended attributes from being modified. Additionally, sensitive fields are excluded from mass assignment by default, ensuring they cannot be manipulated through bulk input. Regular code reviews are also conducted to identify and mitigate potential vulnerabilities related to mass assignment.

We ensure that logs do not contain secrets or Personally Identifiable Information (PII) thorough code reviews. During the review process, we verify that sensitive data like passwords, API keys, and PII are not logged. Developers are guided by best practices and logging guidelines that focus on excluding confidential information

At our company, only the development team has access to customer data, and this is done through a secure VPN that requires multi-factor authentication (MFA) for access. This layered security approach ensures that only authorized personnel can reach sensitive data, further protecting it from unauthorized access.

At our company, only the development team has access to customer data, and this access is strictly controlled through a secure VPN. Access is limited to necessary personnel, ensuring data is handled responsibly and securely. Regular audits and monitoring are conducted to maintain compliance and data protection standards.

To prevent XSS, we use DOMPurify before accepting input in the backend. Input is validated to allow only expected formats, and special characters (e.g., ``, `&`) are encoded into safe HTML entities. Contextual escaping and libraries like OWASP’s ESAPI enhance protection.
To protect against CSRF, use anti-CSRF tokens in forms and API requests, ensure tokens are unique per session.

In case of a security breach, I will notify monday.com immediately upon detection. I will reach out through their developer support or report the issue via Monday’s support email. The notification will include critical details such as when the breach was discovered, the affected data, and steps already taken to contain it.

Here’s a concise 5-step process for installing application-level updates and security patches:

1. Identify and Assess: Regularly check for updates from vendors and review release notes. Assess the impact on your system’s compatibility and functionality.

2. Backup: Create a complete backup of your system, including databases and configurations, ensuring you can restore if issues arise.

3. Test: Apply the update in a staging environment to identify and resolve potential issues before applying it to production.

4. Deploy: Schedule and execute the update during off-peak hours to minimize disruption. Monitor the deployment process for any problems.

5. Verify and Document: After the update, verify that the application works correctly and monitor system performance. Update documentation to reflect the changes and inform stakeholders of any new features or adjustments.

Integrate anything to monday.com - Genie AI transforms the way you manage tasks by automating the creation of monday.com items directly from your emails and their attachments. Whether you're dealing with invoices, contracts, or customer requests, Genie AI extracts the key information you need and converts it into actionable tasks, all with the power of AI.

🔍 Key Features:

AI-Powered Task Creation: Genie AI uses advanced AI to extract data from emails, PDFs, and images, and automatically creates tasks in your monday.com boards.

Versatile Data Extraction: Extract data from the email body, PDF attachments, or images. Simply send an email to your AI agent, and let Genie AI do the rest.

Save & Manage Attachments: Save files to the agent’s comments, with AI-generated notes for additional context.

🚀 Benefits:

Streamlined Workflows: Automate tedious process of task creation, freeing up your team to focus on what matters most.

Increased Accuracy: Reduce human error by relying on AI to extract and populate task details.

Seamless Integration: Works effortlessly within your existing monday.com setup, enhancing your current workflow.

💡 Use Cases:

Invoice Processing: Automatically extract invoice details like due dates, amounts, and supplier information to create tasks for your finance team.

Custom System Integration: Bridge the gap between systems without direct integrations -if it can send an email, Genie can extract the data and create tasks.

Customer Support: Capture customer requests sent via email, converting them into actionable items on your boards.

Set Up AI Agents: Assign a unique email address to each agent and configure extraction prompts for each column.

Review & Optimize: Preview the extraction and refine prompts as needed.

Keep your data up-to-date across multiple boards with Smart Mirror Column, part of the Smart Columns Suite. This app allows you to sync data between Mirror and Standard columns on your monday.com boards, ensuring real-time updates and consistent information across platforms. Whether you're managing multiple teams, collaborating across departments, or just keeping track of data across boards, Smart Mirror Column helps you stay organized and in sync.

  • Automate Workflows: Use mirrored data to trigger formula columns, automate tasks, and create more flexible workflows.

The Smart Columns Suite is a collection of powerful apps designed to enhance your monday.com boards, turning everyday columns into smarter, more efficient tools. From managing data integrity to automating workflows, each app in the suite is crafted to address specific operational challenges, making your team’s work more seamless and productive.


With the Smart Columns Suite, you gain access to multiple apps that work together to solve complex problems, all while ensuring flexibility and ease of use. Best of all, when you purchase any app in the suite, you have the access to the entire suite — ensuring you have all the tools you need to optimize your workflow across the board and you are safe from the hassle of buying many independent apps.

Whether you're a small entrepreneur or part of a larger company, Factura+ integrates seamlessly with monday.com, streamlining your invoicing process to ensure accuracy and compliance.


What will you get with Factura+?


- Full CFDI Management: Issue, cancel, and store electronic tax receipts (CFDI 4.0) effortlessly, all from your monday.com boards.


- Multi-company support: Manage invoices from multiple companies in one place with ease.


- Payment Complements and Credit Memos: Issue Payment Complements and Credit Memos directly through the app.


- Real-time Synchronization: Automations update invoice statuses and move items to the right groups as they are processed.


- Customizable Workflows: Whether you issue one or multiple products/services per invoice, Factura+ adapts to your needs with options for single or multi-item invoicing.


Problems we solve:


- Compliance: Factura+ ensures your invoices comply with SAT regulations.


- Efficiency: Automate your entire invoicing workflow to save time and reduce human error.


- Organization: Keep all invoices, payment complements, and credit memos in one place, fully integrated with your monday.com boards.


Example use case:

A small business can issue a compliant electronic invoice with multiple products or services. Once the invoice is generated, it’s automatically updated, stored, and sent to the SAT for validation, ensuring a smooth workflow with minimal manual intervention.


Ready to simplify your invoicing?

Book a demo here! or leave your details here and we’ll get back to you to show how Factura+ can work for your business!

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: AWS
hello@shadebridge.com
We are not HIPAA-compliant as our application does not store or process private health information (PHI).

We are certified with SOC 2 Type 1 compliant, demonstrating our commitment to maintaining a high standard of security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy in accordance with industry best practices.
Yes we are compliant with the European General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) laws.
As an automation app without a user interface, the only redirection required is to monday.com for authentication purposes, ensuring a secure and trusted destination.

We utilize GraphQL with strongly typed models to securely modify data, ensuring that any unexpected inputs to strongly typed attributes are ignored. Additionally, we implement Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) to manage data efficiently and further mitigate risks.

All code pull requests are subjected to a rigorous approval process, which includes a thorough review of log content. Additionally, the team employs techniques to obscure or redact any data that might contain sensitive or confidential information, ensuring security and privacy throughout the development lifecycle.
Access to customer data is strictly limited to Support and Development team leads, ensuring that only authorised personnel with essential responsibilities can access this information.
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all employees accessing systems that process or store customer data, including AWS, to ensure enhanced security and protect sensitive information.

Yes, our app implements comprehensive encoding and sanitization measures to safeguard against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. Built on a Node.js backend with the Express framework, we leverage the Zod library to validate and sanitize all incoming user inputs. This ensures that any potentially harmful data is filtered and encoded during request processing, effectively mitigating XSS risks and protecting both the application and user data.

Our app is hosted on monday code and the management of the application infrastructure is the responsibility of the monday team. Also, our application data, stored in AWS, is safeguarded by an advanced alarm and monitoring system that continuously oversees our application and infrastructure. In the event of suspicious activity or a potential security breach, the system promptly triggers an alert to notify the development team. This allows the team to swiftly investigate the issue, implement corrective measures, and, if required, notify monday.com about the breach. This proactive monitoring approach ensures timely threat detection and resolution, minimizing risks to our service and customer data.

Our service leverages Dependabot to automate the management of application-level updates and security patches for software packages and databases. Dependabot continuously monitors dependencies, creating pull requests for both routine updates and critical security fixes. High-priority updates, such as those addressing critical or severe vulnerabilities, are reviewed and implemented immediately to maintain system security and stability. For lower-priority updates, our team follows a scheduled approach, reviewing and applying them at regular intervals to ensure the service remains current while maintaining operational efficiency and resource balance.

We ensure data segregation by incorporating an account ID and user ID fields in all entities and enforcing strict filters based on this ID for every request. This approach guarantees that data access is isolated and restricted to the corresponding account, maintaining data integrity and security across the application.

marketplace_apps.description:
The AllDayIT Speedometer App is a versatile dashboarding tool that displays totaled or averaged column values and their targets in a multi-dialed Speedometer gauge.


See other videos about Speedometer at https://www.youtube.com/@AllDayIT-n1y


Main features

  • The main dial displays a column’s total or average, while the second and third different colored dials display the Target and Stretch Target respectively for added performance context.
  • Numbers columns (all pricing plans), as well as Mirror and Formula columns* (paid pricing plans) can be totaled.

*Certain considerations and limitations currently exist for Mirror and Formula columns - see the User Guide for more details

  • The widget can be used in a single board’s chart tab, or in a Dashboard monitoring values across multiple boards and groups.
  • Values and percentages are indicated numerically along the speedometer scale, as well as in a legend below the Speedometer.
  • Get the whole picture by displaying multiple Speedometers in a Dashboard for different KPIs or tracked values. With the Speedometer app, it's easy to monitor large multidimensional projects.


Flexible Pricing Plans

  • Unlimited plan - open to all account users
  • Allowed User based plans - for smaller teams within a larger organization.


Customizability

  • The speedometer features a customizable five-section colored heatmap scale.
  • Text labels (also color-customizable) can be added to each scale section
  • Toggle abbreviation of large numbers
  • Show or hide percentage tick-marks underneath the colored scale.


Use Case Example

Your organization is raising money for a charitable cause. You are accepting pledges via a monday.com WorkForm, and they gather on your main Donations board.

The Speedometer can total up the pledges, with the Target and stretch Target dials letting your team know whether or not your goals are being achieved.

One column over, the actual donations are entered. Another speedometer widget, please just alongside the Pledges speedometer, can Total those up, with Target and a stretch Target giving great goal achievement context there as well.


No matter how you display it, no Dashboard is complete without the AllDayIT Speedometer!


Book a demo with AllDayIT to find out more about the Speedometer app!

Yes, the app protects against mass parameter assignment attacks by implementing strong parameter filtering and whitelisting. Only explicitly permitted fields are allowed to be updated when handling user input, preventing unauthorized or unintended attributes from being modified. Regular code reviews are also conducted to identify and mitigate potential vulnerabilities related to mass assignment.

We ensure that logs do not contain secrets or Personally Identifiable Information (PII) thorough code reviews. compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: Yes, the developer periodically conducts penetration testing to identify and address potential security vulnerabilities, ensuring the application remains secure and resilient against threats.

Yes, the developer has a dedicated security and privacy point of contact to address any issues or questions related to security and privacy.
Security contact email: security@bustbrainlabs.com
Yes, the developer ensures that application logs do not contain secrets or personally identifiable information (PII) to maintain data security and privacy.
Full access to the data is restricted to the CTO and is secured through the use of an encrypted key and a secure connection.
Access to systems that process or store customer data is secured through authentication using a secure private key.

PDF Maker - Automate Documents interface is developed using React.js, which inherently addresses most common XSS vulnerabilities. In PDF Maker - Automate Documents, there are no scenarios where users can or need to generate HTML, making HTML sanitization unnecessary in our user interface.

Templates are created in Google Docs using placeholders that are replaced with actual board data during processing. PDF Maker - Automate Documents performs this replacement using a defined pattern without storing any data in a data source. Additionally, all placeholders are validated using specific REGEX patterns to ensure they are valid and to prevent the insertion of malicious code into the document. Similarly, filenames provided by users are validated against REGEX patterns to exclude unsupported characters, ensuring the security and integrity of the application.
We implement CSRF tokens to validate and secure all incoming requests.

In the event of a security breach, we will promptly notify monday.com via email as soon as the scope of the breach is identified. Additionally, we will directly contact our monday.com representatives through the platform.
Critical patches are applied immediately upon issue identification. High vulnerabilities are addressed within a week, medium vulnerabilities within a month, and low vulnerabilities within a quarter
Yes, customer data is segregated from the data of other customers, either logically or physically, to ensure data isolation and maintain security.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: We store minimal necessary data for an application to function correctly and to support our users.
Cloudflare Logs
Cloudflare D1
In house testing
contact@workflow-boost.com
N/A - the application doesn't store any user health information.

We are not independently SOC-certified, but we follow industry best practices for security, privacy, and data protection. Our hosting provider, Cloudflare, holds SOC 2 certification, ensuring the underlying infrastructure meets strict standards.

We only store personal information required to support the users (basic subscription information including email and name of user installing an app). As a European company, we are obligated to comply with GDPR.
The app redirects only within our trusted domain (*.workflow-boost.com).

Only the CEO can access customer data.
The frontend application is written using the React framework which prevents XSS attacks (we ensure no unsafe methods are used).
The backend application includes CSRF protection middleware ensuring only whitelisted origins can send requests.
Upon discovering a security breach, monday.com support team would be notified.
The application is periodically reviewed to identify security issues with external dependencies. Upon discovery, fixes are applied and released.
QR Flow follows the multi-tenant architecture logically separating all the customer data to prevent any interference between data.

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: orenr@moveo.co.il
We are not compliant with HIPAA as we do not store private
As an app without UI we only need to re-direct the user to monday.com for authentication purposes.

We leverage GraphQL with robustly typed models to modify data, ensuring anything sent to the strongly typed attributes is disregarded. Additionally, we employ DTOs (Data Transfer Objects) for efficient data management.
All code Pull Requests undergo an approval process that includes examining the log content. The team also uses methods to obscure any data that might contain confidential details.
multi-factor authentication is enforced on employees on all the systems which processes/hold customer data (Mongo DB, AWS)
Only the Support and Development team leads have restricted access to customer data.

Yes, our app employs encoding and sanitization on all user-supplied parameters to protect against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. Using Node.js with the Express framework as our backend, we utilize the mongo-sanitize package to sanitize all incoming requests. This approach ensures that any potentially malicious input is appropriately filtered and encoded to prevent XSS vulnerabilities.

By incorporating this sanitization step in our request handling process, we provide a secure environment and minimize the risk of XSS attacks, thereby safeguarding both our application and user data.
Not relevant

Our app is hosted in AWS, includes an alarm and monitoring system designed to alert the development team in the event of a security breach. The system continuously monitors our application and infrastructure, and if it detects any suspicious activity or potential breach, it triggers an alarm to notify the team immediately.

Once alerted, the development team can quickly investigate the issue, take corrective action, and inform monday.com of the breach if necessary. This proactive approach helps ensure that potential threats are addressed swiftly to minimize impact on our service and customers.

Our service utilizes Dependabot to manage application-level updates and security patches for our software packages and databases. Dependabot automatically checks for updates and generates pull requests for package dependencies, including both application-level updates and security patches.

For critical and high-severity updates, we prioritize immediate action. Once Dependabot identifies these updates, our team promptly reviews and applies them to maintain the security and stability of our service.

For other, lower-priority updates, we manage them on a scheduled basis. Our team reviews and applies these updates at regular intervals to ensure that the service remains up-to-date while balancing resource allocation and operational continuity.
We separate data by including an account id field in all entities and applying filters based on it for all requests

compliance_answers.detailedAnswer: The app data is stored in our application database. While we are based in the Netherlands, the data itself is securely hosted in Germany (Frankfurt).
We ensure that application logs do not contain any personal information or secrets. Proper logging practices are in place to prevent the inclusion of sensitive data.
All of our systems enforce multi-factor authentication, including the application database, cloud infrastructure, and source code repository, to ensure secure access and protect customer data.

The application was designed to store as little sensitive information as possible. Therefore, we do not store any of your Google contacts data. We only store the information necessary to provide our services, for example the item IDs and resource names to create a mapping between monday.com and Google Contacts.

Access to this data follows the principle of least privilege. Role-based access controls and authentication mechanisms are in place to prevent unauthorized access and protect your data.
Customer data is logically segregated based on the Account ID. When necessary, further segregation is implemented using the User ID and Board ID to ensure proper data isolation.

Instead, all data is securely housed and managed through the monday.com platform, which fully complies with HIPAA requirements. By leveraging monday.com for data storage, we ensure that all user information is handled in accordance with HIPAA standards.

While Dashboard Formula Widget itself has not undergone independent SOC 2 or SOC 3 certification, it operates exclusively within monday.com's infrastructure, which maintains these certifications. We do not operate separate servers or databases that would require additional certification. By relying on monday.com's certified platform for all data processing and storage, our app maintains the security and compliance standards established by monday.com's SOC certifications.

Dashboard Formula Widget processes and stores data exclusively within the monday.com environment and uses only minimal read permissions. Since we do not process or store personal data outside the monday.com platform, we benefit from the GDPR compliance of the monday.com infrastructure.

Yes, Dashboard Formula Widget is protected against mass parameter assignment attacks. Users cannot directly edit or add parameters. Instead, the app generates a predefined selection from which users can only choose via checkboxes. This ensures that only authorized parameters can be used.

Yes, we ensure our logs do not contain personally identifiable information or sensitive data. Our logging practice is limited to technical error information (e.g., API errors when retrieving data) and contains no user data.

Yes, we strictly follow the principle of least privilege. Dashboard Formula Widget only requests the OAuth scope "board:read," which represents the minimum permissions required for functionality. We never access more data than necessary for our app's core functionality.

Yes, Dashboard Formula Widget implements comprehensive sanitization of all user inputs. We enforce character limits and our validation functions prevent malicious code injection. Input data is properly validated before being stored in the monday.com storage system, ensuring protection against XSS attacks.
Yes, we have a clear process for promptly notifying monday.com in the unlikely event of a security breach to ensure quick and appropriate responses.

glenn.coward@capabilitysource.com

The parameters for the database sync are assigned within the application itself, no user input affects them. They have hardcoded specific columns that they are updating. Our forms on the frontend have only specific fields to be updated as well.
We are using only generic error messages, and not specific secrets, request data or response data for error messages
No one has access to customer data since we are not storing any customer data in our service.
In React.js all of the inputs are sanitized by default, the only problem occurs when the app is using dangerouslySetInnerHTML, which we are not using.

The only state changing request that a user can trigger are the ones modifiying their monday.com instance/workspaces/boards. Here we are using the short lived token from the trigger output or the token from the sdk on the frontend. As such they are both verified with their signing and client secrets before initiating any modifications, and behaving as CSRF tokens in that matter.
We would contact monday.com immediately through an email and describe the situtation and our next steps in resolving the issue.

marketplace_apps.description:
Oboard's Long Description + Rich Text

monday OKR App by Oboard is an intuitive and powerful platform that aligns teams and helps them achieve shared goals.

Seamlessly integrated with monday.com, OKR Board simplifies goal-setting and progress tracking across the organization.

Oboard's OKR monday app allows you to move past time-consuming spreadsheets or the basic monday OKR template. It offers a user-friendly interface and robust features to ensure your team is aligned and ready to achieve strategic goals.


Key Features:

  • Strategy Map. Cascade your OKRs across the organization and connect every goal to the company strategy.
  • Customizable Dashboards: Tailor your OKR views and reports to match team priorities and organizational goals.
  • Visual Roadmaps: Break down yearly OKRs into manageable quarterly objectives and align team efforts.
  • Multi-tool Integration: Connect Jira, monday.com, Salesforce, and other tools via API for unified goal tracking.
  • OKR Check-in Reminders: Connect Microsoft Teams, Slack, and Discord for timely notifications.
  • Outcome-focused Management: Keep teams aligned with actionable insights and comprehensive performance reports.
  • Private Workspaces: Manage data-sensitive projects with secure access controls.
  • Flexibility in OKR setup. Adapt the app to your needs, from adjustable OKR levels, confidence levels, and cycles to custom OKR fields.
  • Web app: monday.com Admins can invite external users who are not part of their monday.com instance. These users will gain access to the Web version of OKR Board, enabling them to collaborate on the same OKRs.

Trusted by over 3,000 companies worldwide, Oboard has already helped customers build more than 100,000 OKRs. Its flexibility accommodates businesses of all sizes, making it the ideal tool for building a collaborative and outcome-driven culture.

Create Invoices Quickly with Flexible Data Entry Options

Tired of manual invoicing? Our app makes it fast and easy to generate professional invoices—whether you enter details manually or import them directly from your boards. Designed for speed, accuracy, and simplicity, our tool streamlines your workflow so you can focus on growing your business.


🔑 Key Features:

✅ Board Integration (Optional) – Instantly import product and order data from your boards for faster, automated invoicing.

✅ Manual Entry Support – Easily input invoice details in a clean, structured format when you prefer full control.

✅ Quick Invoice Creation – Generate invoices in just a few clicks.

✅ Professional Templates – Choose from sleek, ready-made designs.

✅ Tax & Shipping Options – Add relevant costs with ease.

✅ Simple, Intuitive Interface – Designed for efficiency without complexity.

💡 Why Choose This App?

  • Flexible Data Entry – Use board data or manual input—whatever fits your workflow.
  • Save Time – Automation options reduce repetitive tasks.
  • Stay Accurate – Structured fields minimize errors.
  • Adaptable for Any Team – Ideal for freelancers, startups, and businesses of all sizes.
  • Organized & Clear – Keep all invoice information tidy and trackable.

Invoicing Made Easy—Your Way

Whether you're working solo or as part of a team, our app adapts to your style. Import from boards, enter manually, or mix both—your invoices, your choice. Stay efficient, accurate, and in control with every invoice you send. 🚀

Board to Presentation 🖥️📊 application enables you to instantly transform your board data into professional PowerPoint presentation with tables, charts and graphs. Designed for those who need to present board data in a clear, visual format, this app simplifies your board reporting.


✨ Features:

  • 📊 Export board data as tables, pie/bar/line/column charts, and bubble graphs
  • 🔄 Save presentation settings as templates for future use
  • 🎯 Export exact selected items from board


🚀 Why choose Board to Presentation?

  • ⏳ Save time and effort: Eliminate the need to manually copy and format board data into presentations
  • 📊 Make data impactful: Transform board data into visually engaging tables, charts and graphs
  • 📢 Streamline reporting: Create presentations faster, perfect for team updates, client meetings, or stakeholder reviews
  • 💡 Boost productivity: Focus on your core message while the app handles the heavy lifting of data visualization


Check out our 🎥 YouTube videos to see our application in action across popular monday.com board themes!


📖 For more details, see our complete app documentation or contact us via our support email or form. You can also book a demo. 📩🎯

marketplace_apps.description:
Online Planning Poker for distributed teams - launch now and have fun with remotely estimating stories

Fun to work with, lots of voting options

Different ways to achieve agreement on the estimation through Regular cards, Fibonacci sequences, T-Shirt cards, Free Scale both for story points and time.

Real-time chat and micro polls

The extension adds real-time chat capabilities to monday.com. Additionally, micro-polls with up/down voting and likes can be created on each chat message to collect opinionated view and mood among the participants.

Customizable appearance

Layout can be customised to your preference. Color scheme, sound volume and card appearance can be adjusted as you like them most.

More details

Scrumpy Poker is an online planning poker application for distributed agile teams with multiple integrations. It runs on mobile, tablet and desktop computers connecting multiple participants in a real-time story estimation session.

  • Real-time collaboration between your employees, contractors and guests, including the monday.com viewers!
  • Operational on any device
  • Supports Mobile for members and guests
  • Regular, Fibonacci, T-Shirt cards with custom story points
  • Estimate with story points and time with cards or a slider
  • Automatically updates item's story points or time
  • Asynchronous and real-time voting
  • Timers for the voting and refinement session
  • Chat
  • Polls

Planning and refinement sessions must be fun, keep everyone involved and provoke collaboration during the estimation. The Scrumpy Poker online application is a great tool for your planning meetings!

Try now and have fun on Scrumpy Poker's Playground without installing!

apps@cloudvandana.com
Copy Files Pro is not typically subject to HIPAA requirements because our operations do not involve the storage or processing of protected health information.
Copy Files Pro secures navigation by allowing redirects only to pre-approved URLs.
Copy Files Pro secures data by strictly filtering user inputs, preventing mass parameter assignment attacks.
We ensure that the app does not log any of the secrets, tokens, or API keys. We only log account Id and type of action performed.
We are storing user data in Azure and using Azure MFA.
Customer data access is restricted to authorized individuals, requiring private credentials and access is granted only when a legitimate business requirement is demonstrated.
We rigorously prevent XSS attacks through strict input validation and up-to-date library usage.
Copy Files Pro authorizes requests using token-based authentication, requiring valid, app-signed tokens to maintain strict access control and data integrity.

In the event of a data breach with potential impact on monday.com, we will provide immediate notification through email and other appropriate channels. We are committed to transparent collaboration, working in close partnership with monday.com to expedite breach resolution and minimize data leakage.

We host and manage our servers on Microsoft Azure, ensuring a secure environment. We implement regular security updates and API key rotations to protect our systems. In response to emerging threats, we prioritize rapid patching and mitigation to minimize potential risks.
Account IDs are used for data separation; they are added to all entities and employed to filter all requests.

Additionally, we employ strict access controls to ensure that only authorized personnel and processes can access the stored data. Regular audits and monitoring further guarantee data integrity and compliance with security protocols. By leveraging AWS services, we ensure scalability, reliability, and a high level of security for all app data.

We securely store log data on our AWS servers, leveraging AWS's industry-leading security infrastructure to ensure data safety and compliance. Logs are encrypted both in transit and at rest using advanced encryption standards. We also implement strict access control policies, ensuring that only authorized personnel can access the stored data. Furthermore, we regularly monitor and audit our systems to maintain the highest level of security and compliance with industry standards. This approach guarantees that log data is handled with the utmost care and protection.

We ensure compliance by implementing robust data protection measures such as secure encryption, strict access controls, and transparent data handling practices. All user data is collected, processed, and stored in accordance with GDPR principles. Additionally, we provide clear and comprehensive privacy policies, and we only process user data for purposes explicitly agreed upon. By leveraging AWS services, which offer GDPR compliance support, we maintain the highest standards of data protection and user privacy.

Yes, our app restricts redirects and forwards to only approved destinations by validating and sanitizing URLs before performing the action. If a redirect to an untrusted or unknown destination is detected, the app issues a warning to the user, ensuring transparency and reducing the risk of phishing or malicious activities. This approach helps maintain security and user confidence.

Yes, the app is designed to protect against mass parameter assignment attacks. By implementing strict parameter whitelisting and using secure coding practices, we ensure that only explicitly authorized parameters are processed. Sensitive fields are guarded against unintended overwrites, and role-based access control further mitigates any risks related to such attacks.

Yes, the developer ensures that application logs do not contain secrets or personally-identifiable information (PII). We only collect account and subscription information necessary for the app’s functionality. All sensitive data is securely encrypted before storage, following stringent security protocols. Additionally, any PII is rendered unreadable through encryption and is not included in application logs. This approach guarantees the privacy and protection of user information while maintaining compliance with industry standards.

Yes, we adhere to the principle of least privilege to protect access to customer data. Using AWS's Identity and Access Management (IAM) services, we ensure that employees and systems have access only to the resources and data required for their specific roles and tasks. Access permissions are carefully assigned and regularly reviewed to minimize risk and avoid unnecessary privileges. This ensures maximum protection of customer data and aligns with industry best practices for secure data management.

Yes, we enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all employee access to systems that process customer data. Leveraging AWS's MFA capabilities, we require an additional layer of verification beyond traditional passwords, such as authentication codes or physical devices. This significantly enhances security and reduces the risk of unauthorized access to sensitive data. By implementing MFA, we uphold stringent security standards to safeguard customer information and ensure accountability.

Absolutely. The app performs comprehensive encoding and sanitization of all user-supplied input to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities. By employing secure libraries and frameworks, all user inputs are validated and encoded prior to rendering. This process ensures that any malicious scripts are neutralized, protecting users from potential exploitation.

Yes, the developer ensures that all state-changing actions are protected against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). This is achieved by implementing CSRF tokens in forms and API requests, validating the token with every state-changing action. Additionally, session management is tightly secured, and proper authentication mechanisms are enforced to prevent unauthorized actions.
